output.brief: The jump in chilled write-offs is mostly an internal problem, not a Haverlow problem. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four in week 31, night pallets wait a median of about 3h50 between unloading and reaching a chiller (it was 44 minutes before). They sit in unrefrigerated dock lanes at 15–17°C. Night-shift write-offs rose from 0.6% to 2.9%, and the rate is the same for Haverlow, Pellridge and own-label. Day-shift write-offs are flat. Haverlow's trailer data, which can't be edited, shows product at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors open. The chambers also held temperature. The warm receipt probe readings were taken after the dock delay, so they don't show how the product left the trailer. Don't raise the chargeback or move volume. Dropping the night probe would hide the problem. Restore the night team to six, or otherwise fix the dock-to-chamber time. Set a maximum dock-to-chamber time and track it weekly from the scan data. Separately, ask Corriebank for its claim-level data to see how much of the credit rise is over-claiming. That part is unproven, and part of the rise may come from the same warming. I'm fairly confident about the main cause, and less sure about the credits.
